name: Death Valley National Park
summary: The hottest, driest, lowest place in North America — a surreal, beautiful desert of salt flats, dunes, and painted hills, two hours off the Strip.

lodging.name: The Ranch or Inn at Death Valley

foodMustTry.name: A cold drink at Furnace Creek

days.label: Day 384 — Below Sea Level
days.summary: Salt flats, dunes, and painted hills.

item.title: Badwater Basin, Zabriskie & Artist's Palette
item.blurb: Stand 282 ft below sea level on the salt flats, catch sunrise at Zabriskie Point, drive Artist's Palette, and see the Mesquite Dunes — go early, it gets brutally hot.

rest.label: Out of the sun
rest.note: Not laziness — strategy. Everyone who knows this park is indoors or in the water between one and five, and the light is flat and white anyway. Go back to Furnace Creek, sit under the tamarisks, and wait for the afternoon to break.

item.title: Sunset at Dante's View

location.name: Dante's View
location.address: Dantes View Rd, Death Valley National Park, CA

item.blurb: A mile straight up from the salt flats you stood on this morning, with Badwater directly below and 11,000-ft Telescope Peak across the valley. The whole park makes sense from here, and at sunset the basin turns gold. Stay for the stars — this is one of the darkest skies in the country.

days.label: Day 385 — East to the Strip
days.summary: Out of the desert and into the neon.

commute.scenicNote: Out past Death Valley Junction and across the Amargosa Valley — barely two hours from the lowest point in North America to the Strip.

stopsAlongWay.title: Amargosa Opera House
stopsAlongWay.blurb: A one-woman opera house in the middle of nowhere, murals painted across the walls by the dancer who ran it for fifty years.
